recipes.name: Cinnamon Coffee Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix
1 (3.4 ounce) package instant butterscotch pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Stir cake mix, vanilla pudding mix, and butterscotch pudding mix together in a medium bowl. Add eggs, oil, and water; mix until well blended.

Stir brown sugar, cinnamon, and nuts together in a separate bowl. Pour half of the batter into the pan, spread evenly. Sprinkle with half of the nut mixture. Cover with remaining batter and sprinkle with remaining nut mixture.

Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, then turn the oven down to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) and bake until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, an additional 35 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cinnamon Coffee Cake
raw_recipe.description: This cinnamon coffee cake recipe is perfectly spiced and easy to make with cake mix and instant puddings. Great for breakfast, brunch, or dessert.

review.reviewBody:
Given how easy it is to throw together this recipe--and how well it always turns out!--I feel that this coffee cake definitely deserves five stars.

The cake batter takes only five or ten minutes to whip up and seems pretty forgiving. Though the recipe calls for one vanilla pudding mix and one butterscotch pudding mix, I've never used the butterscotch (since I never have any in the cupboard!). Instead, I've used two vanilla mixes or one vanilla and one chocolate mix. Either way, the cake has always turned out great. Also, for a little extra flavor dimension, I've added a couple tablespoons of espresso or instant coffee to the water. The addition of coffee gives the cake a nice, subtle bite--and makes it into a true 'coffee cake.'

Overall, this is a moist, yummy recipe that my family members always ask for. And because it's so easy to make, this would be a great cake for beginning bakers. Thank you, Janis, for your tasty submission!

HELPFUL TIPS AND WHY THIS IS 5 STARS: Everyone is right! This literally takes 5 minutes to throw together and then you've got an entire family excited you made something so pretty (submitted pic). For optional icing/toping, I put 1/2C powdered sugar and 1T of milk in a ziplock bag, cut off corner, and pour over. Looks real pretty and it's only enough to zig zag over. DEFINITELY take the advice of using Duncan Hines cake mix (white or yellow) or one that doesn't already have pudding in it. My oven is fast, and I still had to bake for 45 min at 325, so definitely check with toothpick! Also, you can use 2 pkgs of vanilla INSTANT pudding or 1 of cream cheese if you don't have butterstotch. I think putting 1/3 off batter, 1/3 off brown sugar mix, 1/3 batter, 1/3 brown sugar mix, then last of batter, last of brown sugar mix is the best. It VISUALLY looks prettier when you cut it (again, see pic), and it also isn't too overwhelming. Plus, any more layers then you don't get to taste the brown sugar mix and that's the best part right? I never put nuts b/c the kids don't like it, but if I did ...I'd use pecans.

I followed another reviewer’s suggestion and made muffins instead of a cake. Substituted 3/4 cup applesauce and 1/4 cup oil instead of the full cup of oil as included in the original recipe. I had too much cinnamon mixture and would use less sugar next time, but keep same amount of cinnamon and walnuts. Tip for walnut chopping: put walnuts in ziploc or reuseable bag and crush with your hands.

This was loved by all- so moist! I used 2 vanilla pudding mixes. Cake mixes today seem to be only 15 .25 oz so I added 1/3 cup flour to make ip some of the difference. My husband can’t have nuts so I left them out. 20 minutes at 350 and only 30 at 325 degrees was perfect for us. I used a 13x9 inch pan! Thank you!

Everyone loves this recipe. I use 1/2 cup oil, layer the batter, brown sugar, chocolate chips, and cinnamon sugar twice. Sometimes I'll add butterscotch chips. People ask for the recipe every time I take it somewhere.

This is the easiest coffee cake recipe and so versatile. I have done a lemon cake version with lemon and vanilla pudding, I have dome strawberry with cheesecake and vanilla, and I changed out the butterscotch pudding for cheesecake and use vanilla. Butterscotch is an overpowering flavor. This is requested from me at every family gathering.

I made this cake for a New Years brunch and it was a huge hit! I used two containers of vanilla pudding (instead of the butterscotch) and added mini chocolate chips instead of the nuts to the cinnamon mixture. I made it in a bundt pan and (forgetting to construct the cake upside down because of the bundt pan) ended up with the extra topping that should have gone on top of the cake. Before serving the cake, I drizzled the top with some melted butter and sprinkled the remaining topping on the cake and it was fantastic!

I made this using 1 box of instant banana pudding and 1 box of pistachio pudding. In place of the walnuts I used pistachios. I made this for a brunch and EVERYONE asked for the recipe. One of the women who took the recipe has made it more than 1/2 dozen times for company and has given out the recipe every time.

Ya, I altered the recipe but if it wouldn't have turned out, I would NOT be reviewing it. This was EXCELLENT. I was so excited I had butterscotch pudding on hand & then whoops, it was cook & serve. I went with the 2 instant vanilla instead. I layered 1/3 batter, 1/3 brown sugar mix, etc. Before I added the last 1/3rd of batter, I added a single layer of frozen raspberries (I'm sure you could use any berry) & topped that with the last 1/3rd of the batter. To the last 1/3rd of the brown sugar mix I added a couple Tbsp of butter & mixed until crumbly & sprinkled over the top. It was absolutely delicious!

I think it was OK but with some adjustments, it could be Great. There is very little brown sugar mix in the middle of the cake and then there is tons of dry brown sugar mix on top. If I try to make this again, I will put MOST of the brown sugar mix in the middle layer and then sprinkle some on the top with butter to create that coffee cake crumble. I would also reduce the bake time, 1 hour is too long and my cake came out dry. I think 40 min at 325 is good.

Used the recipe (only changes are: I couldn’t find butterscotch instant pudding, so used 2 vanillas and no nuts) and it turned out great. Adults and kids loved it / everyone wanted seconds. I use a Bundt pan, so I start with the brown sugar / cinnamon mix and then alternate from there. Overall, it’s delicious and super easy!

This cake was super sweet and tasted fine, but I wouldn’t categorize it as a coffee cake. It was easy to make and I made zero substitutions or changes. My teens have been enjoying it as a snack because it is too sweet for breakfast.

Made this for a friend's birthday party and it came out great! I added semisweet chocolate chips to the batter and everyone loved it. Was told to start a baking Instagram, quit my day job, etc. Requested for future events. Highly recommend!
This is my all-time favorite coffee cake recipe! Everyone that tries this loves it!!!! The butterscotch pudding adds amazing flavor, so don't skip it!!!!

I chose this for ease and because it wasn't too dairy-laden, as our granddaughter is lactose intolerant. I was nervous about the intensity of the negative reviewers' comments, even though most people liked it. But it turned out great! Not sure what's going on with this recipe, but everyone at our gathering found the flavor, consistency and sweetness level really enjoyable. It is true that this cake is dense and moist, so not as crumbly and light as a more traditional coffee cake. If that's a deal breaker for you, then don't make this one. But there was no sense of an artificial flavor. Maybe that's about what mixes are used? I'd absolutely make this again.

I make this often. I make it just like the recipe stated. Sometimes, I can't find instant butterscotch pudding and substitute the one that you have to cook. I don't cook it. I just add it the same way and it comes out fine. My family likes this anytime of day. I have made it for a brunch and it was a big hit. It is super moist. Everyone seems to love it. I recently started using gluten free cake mix. It still comes out fantastic and you would never know it was gluten free. I still make it the same way, just with gluten free cake mix.
Like the ease of a cake mix and pudding to enhance the boxed cake

Update to original review: I made this yesterday and this time added 1/4 cup of flour instead of the extra cake mix as I didn't have one. I used the vanilla pudding plus three zero sugar 1 oz butterscotch puddings- all instant. It turned out even better and more dense as it probably should be. Also, their was no aftertaste using the zero sugar puddings but it made me feel a little better as this is such a sweet dessert. Wonderful and very very sweet! Because cake mixes are not 18.25 oz anymore, they are 15.25 oz, I got a tip from a woman who said to add the difference from another cake mix. Just three ounces or so. That way it will come out correct. Otherwise it might be too mushy. Also, I find it most difficult to find instant butterscotch pudding in my stores. So I tried cook and serve for both and it worked just fine.
Needs more cinnamon and extra flour (1/3 cup?) to standard cake mixes.
